transcript.text:
“Not working” can range from a simple socket, control-lock or clock setting issue to a door-switch or internal fault. First, is it completely dead — no display, light or buttons — or does it power up but fail to start or fail to heat? 1. With the microwave unplugged, check the plug is fully in and the wall socket is switched on. Test that socket with another appliance if safe to do so. If the socket is dead, it is a supply issue rather than the microwave.
2. If the socket works, plug the microwave back in and check whether a lock/key symbol is showing. Many models unlock by holding Stop/Cancel for a few seconds; some also need the clock set before they will start.
3. Do not remove the microwave casing or try to inspect its internal fuse: microwave high-voltage parts can retain a dangerous charge even when unplugged. Tell me whether it is dead, powers up but will not start, or starts but does not heat, and I can narrow this down.
It's got power, display shows the time and it beeps, but won't start. There's a little L symbol on the display too.

The little “L” is very likely the control/child-lock symbol. That would explain why the clock and beeps work but it will not start. 1. Try holding the Stop/Cancel button for about 3–5 seconds. If there is a button with a lock or key symbol, hold that instead. On some microwaves the lock clears with a beep and the “L” disappears.
2. Then put a cup of water inside, set 30 seconds and press Start. If the L clears but it still will not run, the next likely cause is the door not being recognised as fully shut. Do not remove the casing or try to bypass any door switch; that needs an engineer if cleaning the accessible door-latch area does not help.
Held the Stop button for 3 secs, the L went away and it works now. Thanks
That was the control/child lock rather than a fault. Holding Stop/Cancel for a few seconds is the usual way to switch it on or off; if it happens again, look for the L/lock symbol first.
